limitations.wanted: a plain, ground Ø8 mm shaft or sleeve for the bearings to run on (a shoulder bolt or a Ø8 tube spacer)
limitations.blocked_by: the hardware list — it has only screws, nuts, washers, heat-set inserts and the salvaged 1/4-20 webcam bolt; no shoulder bolts, no unthreaded sleeves, no tube stock
limitations.why: a 608 bearing is meant to run on a smooth shaft. A catalog M8 screw is threaded over its whole usable length, so the inner races would sit on thread crests with roughly 0.1 mm of radial play and can brinell/creep; the wheel will work, but it will be slightly loose and may get noisier over time

limitations.wanted: measured values for the broken wheel (exact outside diameter, exact width, tread cross-section) and for the door bracket (clear gap between its plates)
limitations.blocked_by: the person couldn't measure them — I got 'about 50 mm across and about 16 mm wide' in words and nothing else, so the tread profile had to be assumed flat and the bracket clearance is unknown
limitations.why: the tread profile (flat vs V vs grooved) and the exact diameter decide whether the new wheel matches the track and whether the door keeps its height; the bracket gap decides whether the wheel's cheeks will rub and whether the nut can clamp the bearing inner races
